title: At the Creation's Birth
description: At the Creation's Birth in Tonic Solfa to SOUTHWELL, doh is Ab: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 1 verses and a piano.
about: John Newton wrote these words. They were printed in Olney Hymns (London, 1779), Book III, hymn 104, “The Father we adore, And everlasting Son; The Spirit of his love and pow'r, The glorious Three in One”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Short Metre (6.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to SOUTHWELL; any other Short Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: At the cre-a-tion's birth This song was sung on high, Shall found, through ev-ery age, on earth, And through e-ter-ni-ty.

lines: This song was sung on high,
Shall found, through every age, on earth,

source: John Newton and William Cowper, Olney Hymns (1779)
licence: Public domain: John Newton died in 1807.
credits: Words by John Newton (1725–1807), public domain, as printed in Olney Hymns (1779); set to SOUTHWELL by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
